what:
Validation-fixture gotcha (2026-04-27, complements #295 + #322): SessionStart auto-injects project-wide preferences + guidelines IDs into `recalled-paths-<sid>.txt` as an `ids|<list>` entry on every new chat session — even a "fresh" Cmd+N chat. This populates tracking BEFORE the user runs any prompts, so a Read on a file whose scoped_ids partially overlap with the injected set gets either soft (encountered + missing) or silent (all covered) instead of hard-block.

**Concrete pattern in /private/tmp/aide-cursor-val on 2026-04-27:**
- SessionStart injects ~10 IDs (project-wide prefs/guidelines + some scoped guidelines like `src/api/** camelCase` (#2), `Unix epoch ms` (#5), `X-RateLimit headers` (#15)).
- Reading `src/api/routes.ts` in a fresh chat: scoped_ids = [2, 5, 6, 7, 14, 15]. Of these, [2, 5, 15] are auto-tracked from SessionStart → only [6, 7, 14] missing. Plus agent likely calls aide_recall proactively per rules-file guidance, which tracks the file path AND covers the remaining IDs → preToolUse:Read fires silently.
- Reading `src/auth/middleware.ts` in same chat: scoped_ids = [1, 4]. Neither is in the injected set. Agent's proactive recall might still cover them, but even without that, the hard-block path is guaranteed to fire on first read.

**Rule for hard-block validation in fresh-fixture testing:**
1. Pick a target file whose scoped memories are ALL technical (technical layer is generally not auto-injected by SessionStart — only preferences + guidelines are by default per #297).
2. AND whose scoped memories' IDs don't overlap with the priority:always or guideline IDs that get injected.
3. AND test in a TRULY fresh Cmd+N chat (Cursor) or new session (Claude Code) — NOT just "Clear" in Cursor (per #357, Clear keeps session_id and tracking persists).
4. The adversarial prompt "without calling aide-memory tools first" doesn't reliably suppress proactive recall — agents often recall anyway per rules-file guidance. So even a "good" target may go soft if agent preempts. To truly force hard-block, also temporarily disable the rules file (mv `.cursor/rules/aide-memory.mdc` aside per #295) OR use a file the agent has no reason to think needs recall yet.

**Diagnostic signal in tracking files:**
- `recalled-paths-<sid>.txt` containing `ids|<list>` entry only → SessionStart fired but no path-Read tracked yet
- Same file additionally containing `file|<absolute-path>` entries → those paths have been encountered (tracked by track-recall.sh on aide_recall calls OR self-track-on-fire by preRead)
- coveredCount > 0 + encountered=true + missing IDs → soft path
- coveredCount = scoped_ids.length → silent path (everything covered)
- coveredCount = 0 + encountered=false → hard block path-based message
- coveredCount > 0 + encountered=false (rare — scoped_ids covered without file being read) → hard block ID-based message

**Pattern for `recalled-paths-<sid>.txt` content shape:** lines are key-prefixed, each line either `ids|<comma-list>` (one such entry total) or `file|<absolute-path>` (one per encountered file). This is the canonical tracking format.
why: User confused by "no chrome on fresh-chat hard-block test" — the actual cause was SessionStart auto-injection populating tracking with overlapping IDs, plus agent's proactive recall. Future validation sessions will hit the same shape if they don't account for the injection-tracking interplay. Captures the file-selection rule (pick technical-only scoped memories with no overlap with injected) so future fixture designs and ad-hoc tests get reliable hard-block triggers. Also documents the diagnostic signals in the tracking file so future log analysis is faster.
